parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, border, facility, or custody exposure is documented, and hate-speech and anti-discrimination law cover gender identity with a generally liberal climate. Risk is concentrated in street/public hostility and imperfect recourse: reported hate crimes rose, clearance fell to 45%, only 8% report, and some reporters face dismissive treatment, despite the Pride shooter receiving the maximum 30 years and threats declining. This places the regime between strong-protection and moderate-friction anchors.

care_services.exposure: Resident referral pathway grants access to about one-quarter, non-binary patients lacked treatment in 2023 report; visitor hormone continuity not documented.
care_services.protection: 2020 guideline states psychiatric assessment is not a precondition and promotes informed consent; sources conflict on practice.
care_services.interaction: Resident restrictions hint at bureaucratic friction but do not document denial to visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Organised anti-trans hostility exists among extremists and religious fundamentalists; tabloid/partisan criticism documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate speech covers transgender people since 2020; anti-discrimination since 2013; prime minister publicly condemns anti-trans hate.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law frames trans people as protected victims, not threats; no state threat-framing documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Visitor-specific minor exposure not documented; resident under-18 care is counselling-centred and drug treatment only via national service.
minors_guardians.protection: Resident legal-gender change from age 16 by self-declaration, 6-16 jointly with parents; this is not a visitor protection.
minors_guardians.interaction: No documented rule affecting a travelling minor or guardian's entry, facilities, or care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2022 Pride mass shooting; knife attack investigated as hate crime; online threats at drag event; hate-crime reports rose 18% in 2023.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Shooter sentenced to 30 years, strictest penalty; security service reports significant decline in threats; dedicated reporting group exists.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Rising reports coexist with falling clearance 52% to 45%, low trust, and dismissive treatment of some reporters.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Only 8% of hate-crime victims report; official figures are a floor and true volume unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Hate-crime recording includes gender identity/expression; courts imposed maximum sentence in Pride case.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Border, facilities, detention, and visitor-care practices are expressly undocumented, so no inference either way is made.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar explicit legal protection and broad tolerance, but this case has weaker documented recourse—45% clearance, 8% reporting, dismissive treatment—so it sits below 0.85.

Similar: protections exist and perpetrators can be prosecuted, yet violence and reporting barriers remain. This case is slightly safer due to max-sentence prosecution, declining threats, and no documented facility/border restrictions.

This case is higher than 0.65 because legal protection is explicit at national level and the most serious attacker received the maximum sentence; uncertainty is mainly about undocumented visitor practices, not documented systemic denial.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: no documented traveller-facing restriction at entry, facilities, or custody, with national law actively protecting gender identity and society comparatively liberal. The operative risk if outed is social hostility, largely organised or online, plus a hate-crime system that prosecutes serious cases but clears fewer than half and is distrusted by victims. Undocumented axes cannot be assumed safe, yet rubric prohibits inferring exposures from absence; documented evidence supports Low-to-Reduced Risk around 0.80, for solo adults and travelling families alike.
